hero.headline: U.S. and Iran sign agreement to end war and reopen Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have signed a memorandum of understanding to end their conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump signed the document remotely, with the agreement now in effect. The signing happened ahead of a scheduled ceremony in Switzerland on Friday, after discussions among mediating countries about implementing the deal sooner.

The 14-paragraph memo includes an end to fighting, a commitment that Iran will never develop nuclear weapons, and a $300 billion redevelopment package for Iran. The deal aims to stabilize global energy markets after two months of military action that severely disrupted energy production and transportation across the Middle East.

Trump defended the agreement during an hour-long press conference, though he appeared to lower expectations for success. He warned he could authorize military strikes against Iran again if nuclear negotiations fail. Critics argue that making concessions simply to return to the pre-war situation demonstrates the conflict itself was a costly mistake. Before the war and as it began, Trump had outlined highly ambitious goals including Iran's total surrender and complete dismantling of its nuclear program.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has sharply criticized the deal, calling it a strategic and political disaster. Netanyahu had promised the Israeli public total victory but now faces Trump's diplomatic settlement and repeated public criticism from the president, occurring four months before an Israeli election. Netanyahu stands alone internationally in his opposition. Even the United Arab Emirates, previously the most hawkish Gulf state, supports the diplomatic resolution. Republican allies in Washington and the media have also been reluctant to fully reject a deal carrying Trump's approval.

The immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz faces significant delays. An estimated 5,000 mines that Iran placed in the waterway during the conflict must be swept before normal shipping traffic can resume. Trump said the U.S. military had already begun searching for mines, but the operation will require considerable time.

The conflict has created widespread economic damage globally. About 20,000 seafarers and 2,000 ships have been stranded in the Gulf. Germany halved its 2026 growth forecast to 0.5 percent on Wednesday, while Greece announced 500 million euros in extra aid for households and farmers. Countries in Asia dependent on Gulf oil have suffered particularly severe shortages of fuel, fertilizer, and other raw materials.

Peace negotiations remain fragile. Iran's parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that reopening the strait would be impossible while the U.S. and Israel committed breaches of the ceasefire, including the U.S. naval blockade. He accused them of "hostage-taking of the world's economy." Iran's military seized two ships attempting to cross the strait on Wednesday, marking the first vessel seizures since the war began on February 28.

cards.headline: B-52 bomber crash at Edwards Air Force Base kills eight
cards.body:
Eight people died when a B-52 Stratofortress bomber crashed at Edwards Air Force Base in the Mojave Desert, about 100 miles northeast of Los Angeles. The aircraft went down during a test flight on Monday with no survivors.

The bomber took off from the California base and made a sharp right turn followed by a near 180-degree turn before plummeting to another runway at a rate of about 5,056 feet per minute, nearly 10 times faster than a typical landing descent. The crash resulted in a fiery explosion that sent thick plumes of smoke across the base.

Those killed included Boeing employees, government workers, military personnel and civilian contractors. Their identities have been released by the Air Force. Among the victims was an engineer marking his wedding anniversary and an Iowa native. One victim was described by his wife as "a leader, he's a hero."

The aircraft was supporting a radar modernization program. In 2025, Boeing delivered a B-52 to Edwards equipped with a modernized radar system designed to keep the bomber operational through at least 2050, nearly a century after it first entered service.

Investigators believe a flight control malfunction likely caused the crash. According to aviation safety expert Jeff Guzzetti, who previously worked for the Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board, "I think it was definitely a controllability issue. Now, whether that was tied to an engine failure, a flight control failure, or some new testing device failure, I'm not sure."

Guzzetti suggested the controls could have been rigged incorrectly after maintenance, or the crash could have resulted from a catastrophic engine problem or failure of equipment being tested. The investigation into the accident could take up to six months to complete, officials said.

Crews worked to make the crash site safe for search and recovery teams after fires flared up overnight. The airfield remained closed on Tuesday.

Edwards Air Force Base has served as a testing and development facility for military aircraft since World War II. The 412th Test Wing runs the base and conducts developmental testing of all Air Force aircraft, weapons systems, software and components before the service purchases them and throughout their operational lifespans.

The crash marks one of several recent fatal military aviation accidents. In 2024, an instructor pilot died when an ejection seat activated while the aircraft remained on the ground in Texas. Two Air Force pilots were killed when a trainer jet crashed near an Alabama airport in 2021. An Air Force ROTC cadet died in a 2022 accident involving a Humvee during a training exercise in Idaho.

cards.headline: Federal Reserve holds rates steady as new chairman signals possible hikes ahead
cards.body:
The Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged at its first meeting under new chairman Kevin Warsh, maintaining rates in a range of 3.5% to 3.75% where they have remained since December. The decision received unanimous support from the voting committee, but signaled a notable shift in the central bank's outlook on future policy.

Stock markets initially declined following the announcement, with the Dow dropping 500 points and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each falling over 1.2%. The reaction reflected investor concerns about the Fed's new direction under Warsh's leadership.

The policy statement highlighted economic concerns, noting that "economic activity is expanding at a solid pace despite elevated uncertainty that owes, in part, to the conflict in the Middle East." Committee members acknowledged that inflation remains elevated at 4.2 percent, well above the Fed's 2 percent target, driven partly by sharp increases in energy prices from the Middle East conflict.

A significant change in expectations emerged from the Fed's latest projections. Nine of the voting members now predict at least one rate increase by year's end, a dramatic reversal from March when 12 of 19 officials projected rate cuts. Warsh notably did not contribute to these projections, making him the sole board member to abstain.

The policy statement itself was notably shorter than previous versions, reflecting Warsh's stated desire to tighten the Fed's public communications. In his first press conference as chairman, Warsh outlined plans for five new taskforces to overhaul the central bank's approach. These groups will examine monetary policy conduct, communications, the balance sheet, data, and productivity and jobs. One taskforce specifically will reassess how the Fed communicates with the public, including news conferences, projections, and meeting transcripts.

Warsh struck a different tone on inflation compared to his earlier reputation as an inflation hawk. He stated that the Fed's monetary policy "cannot have a very significant effect on particularly prices," noting that oil, eggs, and beef prices "do not have first-order consequences to what we're doing." However, he emphasized the Fed's role in preventing such price increases from spreading throughout the broader economy.

The situation presents challenges for the new chairman. Inflation has reached its highest level since 2023, while hourly earnings have dropped to 0.7 percent, suggesting wage gains have been eroded by price increases. Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, has risen more modestly to 2.9 percent. The labor market remains relatively strong with unemployment at 4.3 percent.

A ceasefire announcement between the United States and Iran sent oil prices to three-month lows, though analysts expect energy prices will take months to fully normalize. Warsh begins his four-year term navigating these economic pressures while establishing the Fed's independence under his leadership.

cards.headline: Senate pressures Defense Secretary Hegseth over Iran school attack and boat strikes
cards.teaser: Lawmakers are increasing demands for answers about apparent incidents during the Iran conflict that the Pentagon has not addressed for months.
cards.body:
Frustrated senators are targeting Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's travel and public schedule as they escalate pressure to obtain information about apparent Iranian attacks on a school and boat strikes during the recent conflict. Lawmakers say they have sought answers for months without receiving responses from the Pentagon.

The standoff reflects growing tensions between Congress and the Defense Department over transparency regarding incidents during the Iran war. Senate members are using their oversight authority to demand accountability from Hegseth on events that occurred during military operations.

cards.headline: Tropical Storm Arthur weakens after Texas landfall but flooding threat continues
cards.teaser: The first named storm of the season made landfall on the Texas coast before weakening.
cards.body:
Tropical Storm Arthur made landfall on the Texas coast as the first named storm of the Atlantic hurricane season. The storm has since weakened and is not expected to strengthen further.

Life-threatening flash floods remain a significant concern along the northern Gulf Coast as the system moves inland. Forecasters are monitoring rainfall totals and flood risks across the affected region.

cards.headline: Iranian mines in Strait of Hormuz delay reopening of shipping lane
cards.teaser: An estimated 5,000 mines placed during the war must be cleared before normal traffic can resume through the critical waterway.
cards.body:
Plans to quickly restore shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz are delayed by thousands of mines Iran placed in the waterway during the conflict. President Trump said the U.S. military had already begun searching for mines, estimating around 5,000 devices were deployed in the strait.

The mine-clearing operation will postpone the return to normal shipping operations despite the memorandum of understanding signed this week to end the war and reopen the critical passage. The strait serves as a vital route for global energy shipments, and the mines present a significant obstacle to implementing the agreement's economic provisions.

cards.headline: Trump Administration AI Restrictions Cause Tension With G7 Allies
cards.teaser: New U.S. limits on access to AI company Anthropic prompted pushback from allied nations during summit meetings.
cards.body:
The Trump administration's restrictions on Anthropic have created friction among U.S. allies at the G7 summit. French President Macron pressed for broader access to AI technology and called for democracies to work together on AI regulation. Anthropic's CEO addressed G7 leaders, urging them to avoid fragmenting global AI governance.

Trump met with AI executives during the summit to discuss international AI rules. Allied leaders worry that unilateral U.S. restrictions could complicate coordinated approaches to AI development among democratic nations.

hero.headline: Russian Strike Damages Historic Ukrainian Monastery in Kyiv
hero.teaser: One of Ukraine's most significant religious sites came under Russian attack, prompting emergency efforts to preserve cultural artifacts.
hero.body:
A Russian strike hit the Pechersk Lavra monastery in Kyiv, one of Ukraine's holiest sites. The attack sparked a fire at the cultural and religious landmark, which holds deep significance for Ukrainian faith and national identity. Emergency teams responded to contain the flames and protect artifacts and structures.

The strike is part of ongoing Russian offensive operations in Ukraine. In response, Ukrainian forces conducted drone strikes on Moscow, hitting an oil refinery in the city's southeastern Kapotnya district for the second time this week and damaging a shopping center. Moscow's mayor said air defenses shot down approximately 180 drones heading toward the capital.

cards.headline: Trump Administration AI Restrictions Cause Tension With G7 Allies
cards.teaser: New U.S. limits on access to AI company Anthropic prompted pushback from allied nations during summit meetings.
cards.body:
The Trump administration's restrictions on Anthropic have created friction among U.S. allies at the G7 summit. Trump met with AI executives during the summit to discuss international AI rules. Allied leaders worry that unilateral U.S. restrictions could complicate coordinated approaches to AI development among democratic nations.

cards.headline: Japan Calls for Military Buildup to Prevent Future Conflicts
cards.teaser: Japanese Defence Minister says the country must reconsider its post-World War II pacifist stance.
cards.body:
Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi has told the BBC that Japan must move away from the pacifist approach that has guided its defense policy since World War II. He argues that increased military capability is essential to preventing conflict in the region.

The statement marks a notable shift in how Japan's defense posture is being discussed publicly. Japan has operated under constitutional constraints on military force since 1945, though growing regional security concerns have sparked broader debate about strengthening the country's defensive capabilities.

cards.headline: Southeast Asian Countries Turn to Solar Power Amid Energy Crisis
cards.teaser: Homeowners and businesses are installing rooftop solar panels to offset soaring costs from oil-dependent energy systems.
cards.body:
Countries across Southeast Asia are accelerating solar panel installation as energy costs surge following the Iran conflict. The region, which relies heavily on imported oil, has seen homeowners and businesses adopt rooftop solar systems to reduce expenses.

The shift to solar energy represents a response to supply disruptions and price increases in global oil markets. The Iran war has contributed to instability in energy costs, prompting countries dependent on oil imports to seek alternative power sources.

cards.headline: Trump Hosted at Versailles Palace During G7 Visit
cards.teaser: French President Macron extended a dinner invitation at the historic palace as part of diplomatic engagement.
cards.body:
President Trump attended a dinner at the Palace of Versailles hosted by French President Macron during the G7 summit. The historic venue provided a setting for diplomatic engagement between the two leaders as the international summit concluded.

As the G7 wrapped up, Trump faced questions at a press conference and touted a tentative agreement reached with Iran during the summit. The preliminary accord outlined a $300 billion plan for Iran's reconstruction and 60 days of negotiations on its nuclear program.

cards.headline: Trump Criticizes Israel While Defending Iran Agreement at G7
cards.teaser: The President defended his Iran deal and made critical comments about Israel as the summit concluded.
cards.body:
President Trump defended the Iran agreement during closing remarks at the G7 summit and made critical statements about Israel, a longtime U.S. ally. Trump denied that the United States would directly fund the $300 billion reconstruction package for Iran outlined in the preliminary accord.

The President compared his agreement with Iran favorably to the 2015 nuclear deal negotiated under President Obama. Trump's comments about Israel marked an unusual public criticism of the ally during an international forum focused on the Iran agreement.

cards.headline: Trump Says He Is 'the Boss' at G7, Expresses Support for Ukraine
cards.teaser: The President made assertive comments about U.S. leadership and indicated backing for Ukraine's objectives.
cards.body:
President Trump declared himself "the boss" during G7 proceedings and expressed support for Ukraine's war aims. The comments came as allied leaders responded positively to the Iran agreement, contributing to what Trump described as improved relations with partner nations.

The President's tone at the summit reflected confidence following allied praise for the preliminary Iran accord. Trump's statements about Ukraine represented a shift in public positioning on the conflict, which has continued with recent Russian strikes on cultural sites in Kyiv.

cards.headline: Warehouse fire in Boyle Heights prompts shelter orders and helicopter response
cards.teaser: A massive fire at a Los Angeles warehouse involving solar panels triggered rare aerial firefighting operations.
cards.body:
A massive fire erupted Wednesday at a 500,000 square-foot cold storage and freezing facility in Boyle Heights, Los Angeles. The solar panel-covered roof of the Lineage-owned warehouse caught fire, releasing thick clouds of dark smoke and ammonia into the air. About 110 firefighters responded to the blaze, with both city and county hazmat teams deployed to contain it.

City officials issued shelter-in-place orders for nearby residents due to the ammonia threat. Firefighters eventually contained the fire, and the shelter-in-place order was lifted once the blaze was controlled.

cards.headline: Georgia Republicans drop redistricting plan after protests
cards.teaser: Republican legislative leaders rejected calls to redraw congressional districts that would have reduced Black representation.
cards.body:
Georgia Republican legislative leaders rejected a redistricting plan that would have reduced Black representation in the state. The decision came after mounting protests and warnings from Democrats. The GOP declined to redraw the congressional map despite calls from the governor for redistricting ahead of the 2028 elections.

The move represents a break with former President Trump, who had supported the redistricting effort. Democrats warned that the fight over voting representation in Georgia is not over. The decision leaves the current congressional district map in place for upcoming elections.

cards.headline: Teen dies after falling from horse-drawn carriage in Central Park
cards.teaser: An 18-year-old tourist was killed when a horse bolted and overturned a carriage near a popular New York City destination.
cards.body:
An 18-year-old tourist died after falling from a horse-drawn carriage in Central Park. The incident occurred when the carriage driver stepped down to photograph the passengers, causing the horse to bolt. The carriage subsequently toppled over.

Horse-drawn carriages are a long-standing attraction in Central Park, offering rides to visitors exploring the Manhattan landmark.

cards.headline: Apple to raise prices as chip costs rise with AI expansion
cards.teaser: The technology company cited increased chip costs driven by artificial intelligence demand.
cards.body:
Apple plans to raise prices on its products as semiconductor costs climb due to surging demand for AI-capable chips. CEO Tim Cook indicated the increases are unavoidable, citing unsustainable memory expenses being passed to the company. Apple has been integrating AI features across its devices and services.

The company has not yet announced when the price increases will take effect or which specific products will be affected.

cards.headline: Austin tech CEO Joshua Baer killed in plane crash near Laredo
cards.teaser: The Capital Factory founder died when a private jet crashed while traveling to Austin.
cards.body:
Joshua Baer, founder and CEO of Capital Factory, died in a plane crash near Laredo, Texas. The private jet was traveling to Austin when it went down. Baer was known as a central figure in Austin's startup community.

Volunteers with sledgehammers and shovels raced to save passengers at the crash site. Baer had been instrumental in building Austin's technology and entrepreneurship scene. Capital Factory serves as a coworking space and startup accelerator in the Texas capital.

cards.headline: Asian stock markets hit record highs following US-Iran peace deal
cards.teaser: Major Asian stock indexes climbed to unprecedented levels as investors responded to the signing of a peace agreement between the United States and Iran.
cards.body:
The Nikkei and KOSPI both reached all-time highs as Asian markets processed the implications of the US-Iran peace deal. The KOSPI surpassed 9,000 for the first time, while the Nikkei also set a new record. Technology stocks led the gains, with SoftBank surging more than 10 percent on optimism about regional stability and economic prospects.

The peace agreement between the United States and Iran has shifted investor sentiment across Asian markets. Traders responded positively to the reduced geopolitical risk, particularly in sectors sensitive to Middle East tensions. The rally came despite mixed signals from Wall Street, where stocks declined following the Federal Reserve's policy decision earlier in the week.

cards.headline: Oil prices fall as energy agency forecasts supply glut after Iran deal
cards.teaser: Crude oil prices dropped after the International Energy Agency projected a significant supply surplus next year following the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
Following the announcement of a US-Iran peace deal, oil prices declined by 2 percent. A key component of the agreement involves reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil shipments that will restore normal supply flows to energy markets.

The International Energy Agency projects a substantial oil surplus as Iranian oil returns to global markets. This shift from recent supply constraints to an expected glut represents a significant reversal driven by the geopolitical settlement between the US and Iran.

cards.headline: SpaceX stock declines for first time since IPO after three-day surge
cards.teaser: Shares of SpaceX fell 6 percent, marking the first drop since the company went public after a rally that pushed the stock up 58 percent.
cards.body:
SpaceX shares dropped 6 percent, marking the first decline since the company's stock market debut. The stock had gained approximately 50 percent following its initial public offering on the Nasdaq, where SpaceX was valued at $2.2 trillion.

The pullback ended a three-day winning streak that had driven strong investor interest in the commercial space sector. The recent decline represents a pause in the rally as trading patterns begin to normalize following the company's highly anticipated market debut.

cards.headline: Apple plans price increases as AI development drives up chip costs
cards.teaser: Apple announced plans to raise prices on its products as demand for artificial intelligence capabilities pushes up the cost of semiconductor components.
cards.body:
Apple will raise prices across its product lineup amid surging chip costs linked to artificial intelligence demand. Outgoing CEO Tim Cook confirmed the price increases but did not specify which products would be affected or when the changes would take effect.

The move reflects intensifying competition among technology companies for advanced semiconductors as chip manufacturers struggle to keep pace with AI hardware demand.

cards.headline: Shipping giant warns against Iran charging fees for Strait of Hormuz passage
cards.teaser: Maersk's CEO cautioned that allowing Iran to impose transit fees on ships using the Strait of Hormuz would establish a dangerous precedent for international shipping.
cards.body:
The chief executive of Maersk expressed concern about provisions in the US-Iran peace deal that could permit Iran to charge fees for vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz. The shipping company executive argued that such an arrangement would set a troubling precedent for global maritime commerce. Maersk is proceeding cautiously as details of the agreement to reopen the Persian Gulf emerge.

The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important shipping chokepoints, and questions about transit arrangements carry significant implications for international trade. Maersk's position reflects broader industry concerns about the terms under which normal shipping operations will resume. The company has not announced specific changes to its routes or operations pending clarification of the final deal terms.

cards.headline: Elon Musk could pursue merger of SpaceX and Tesla, legal experts say
cards.teaser: Legal analysts suggest Elon Musk may seek to combine SpaceX and Tesla in a major corporate merger, though shareholders could face limited options to object.
cards.body:
Elon Musk's next major business move could involve merging SpaceX and Tesla into a single entity, according to legal experts analyzing his corporate strategy. Such a combination would unite his electric vehicle company with his space exploration venture in what would rank as one of the largest corporate mergers in recent years. Experts noted that while some shareholders might oppose the deal, their ability to block it could be limited.

The speculation comes as SpaceX completes its initial public offering and establishes a public market valuation. A merger would give Musk control over a combined company spanning transportation on Earth and in space. Legal analysts pointed to Musk's ownership stakes and voting power in both companies as factors that could enable such a transaction despite potential shareholder resistance.

hero.headline: Apple to raise iPhone prices due to memory chip shortage
hero.body:
Apple's chief executive Tim Cook has announced that the company plans to raise prices across its product lineup in response to escalating memory chip costs driven by artificial intelligence development.

In recent remarks, Cook indicated that price increases are now unavoidable. He explained that the company has been attempting to absorb the substantial cost increases being passed down by component suppliers, but the situation has become unsustainable. Rather than continuing to shield customers from these expenses by reducing profit margins, Apple has decided that price rises are necessary.

The memory chip shortage stems from unprecedented demand for high-performance computing components as technology companies race to incorporate artificial intelligence features into their devices. Apple's strategy to expand AI capabilities within its products, particularly in Siri, requires significantly more memory than previous generations. The upcoming iPhone 18 is expected to include 12 gigabytes of RAM to support these enhanced features, roughly double the amount found in many current models.

The shortage has created intense competition among technology manufacturers for limited supplies from major producers. Samsung and SK Hynix control much of the global memory chip production, and their output cannot meet current demand. Multiple smartphone makers are simultaneously rushing to add generative AI functionality to their devices, further straining available inventory.

Cook did not specify which products would be affected by the price increases or provide details about how much prices would rise. He also declined to announce when the increases would take effect. This marks a notable departure from Apple's historical approach. The company has traditionally maintained stable pricing even during periods of component shortages by absorbing the additional costs internally or adjusting profit margins downward.

Industry analysts have observed that memory chip supply constraints have deteriorated significantly over the past year as AI applications have driven unprecedented demand for high-performance components. The timing of Apple's announcement is significant as the company prepares to introduce new iPhone models later this year that will heavily feature AI capabilities to differentiate themselves from previous versions.

The price increases could affect Apple's competitive standing in the smartphone market, where the company already charges premium prices compared to most Android manufacturers. Consumers have grown accustomed to Apple's flagship devices commanding high prices, but further increases could push some buyers toward alternative options, particularly if competing manufacturers manage to offer advanced AI features without proportional price hikes.

Cook's comments represent one of the first major admissions from a technology leader that the artificial intelligence boom is creating genuine financial pressures on device manufacturers. The announcement signals that the cost of developing and implementing AI features will likely be passed on to consumers through higher prices rather than absorbed by companies seeking to maintain market share.

cards.headline: NASA partners with private sector on Mars science missions
cards.teaser: NASA announced a new public-private partnership aimed at advancing scientific research on Mars.
cards.body:
NASA has established a public-private partnership to advance Mars science research. The space agency announced the collaboration, which will bring together government resources and private sector capabilities for future Mars exploration efforts.

The partnership represents NASA's continued strategy of leveraging commercial partnerships to expand its planetary science capabilities. The agency has increasingly relied on private companies to supplement its exploration programs as it pursues ambitious goals for Mars research and eventual human missions to the planet.

cards.headline: Archaeologists discover 5,000-year-old structure near Stonehenge
cards.teaser: Researchers found a simpler precursor to Stonehenge located three miles from the famous monument.
cards.body:
Archaeologists have discovered a 5,000-year-old monument near Stonehenge that may have served as a prototype for the famous site. Located at Bulford, three miles from Stonehenge in Wiltshire, the structure was aligned with the summer and winter solstices and has been carbon dated to around 3000 BC.

The discovery coincides with the earliest phase of Stonehenge's construction, predating the placement of the monument's massive trilithon stones by approximately 500 years. Experts have called the find a "once in a lifetime" discovery, suggesting it provides insight into how ancient peoples tracked seasonal changes through solar observation.

cards.headline: FDA approves second fly species for medical maggot therapy
cards.teaser: Regulators cleared another carcass-eating fly for use in treating wounds with maggot therapy.
cards.body:
The Food and Drug Administration has approved a second species of fly for maggot therapy used to treat certain types of wounds. The therapy involves using fly larvae to clean dead tissue from wounds, a practice that has been used in medicine for decades.

Maggot therapy has supporters in the medical community despite limited robust clinical data on its effectiveness. The larvae consume dead tissue while leaving healthy tissue intact, making them useful for treating certain chronic wounds and infections.

cards.headline: Redesigned lobster traps aim to reduce bycatch deaths
cards.teaser: Fishing equipment manufacturers are adding escape hatches to lobster pots to protect unintended marine life catches.
cards.body:
Commercial fishing equipment is being redesigned to reduce bycatch, the unintended capture of marine creatures in lobster traps. New designs incorporate escape hatches that allow non-target species to exit the traps while retaining lobsters.

The modifications address a problem affecting thousands of marine animals that become trapped in lobster pots each year. The redesign effort seeks to make commercial lobster fishing more sustainable by reducing its impact on other marine species.

cards.headline: Google adds option to disable AI features in Docs
cards.teaser: Users can now turn off AI-powered writing suggestions that appear in Google Docs.
cards.body:
Google has provided a way for users to disable artificial intelligence features in Google Docs, including the prompts to write with Gemini that appear during document creation. The company added settings that allow users to opt out of the AI-powered writing assistance.

The change addresses user feedback about unwanted AI suggestions appearing while writing. Users can access the settings to remove the pop-up prompts and other AI-generated writing recommendations from their document editing experience.

cards.headline: International Space Station crew photographs aurora over South Pole
cards.teaser: Astronauts aboard the ISS captured footage of aurora australis dancing beneath the station.
cards.body:
Astronauts on the International Space Station recorded video of a glowing aurora australis display over the South Pole. The footage shows the southern lights moving beneath the orbiting station, providing a view of the atmospheric phenomenon from above.

The aurora displays occur when charged particles from the sun interact with gases in Earth's atmosphere. The International Space Station's orbit allows astronauts to observe these light shows from a unique vantage point above the atmosphere where the phenomena occur.

hero.headline: Ghana scores in stoppage time to defeat Panama in World Cup opener
hero.body:
Ghana secured a dramatic victory over Panama in their World Cup opener in Toronto, Canada, with Caleb Yirenkyi scoring a goal in the 95th minute. The late strike denied Panama their first-ever point in World Cup competition and gave Ghana all three points to start their tournament campaign.

The match appeared headed for a draw until the final moments of stoppage time when Yirenkyi found the back of the net. Panama, making their second World Cup appearance after debuting in 2018, came close to achieving a historic result before the heartbreaking conclusion. The Central American nation had defended throughout the match in search of their maiden World Cup point.

Ghana returned to the World Cup after missing the previous tournament. The African nation previously reached the quarterfinals in 2010 and has been a regular participant in the competition. The late winner provides important momentum as teams navigate the expanded 48-team format introduced for this World Cup.

The victory gives Ghana three points in their opening group stage match. Teams compete in groups during the first round of the tournament, with the top finishers advancing to the knockout stages. Opening match results carry significant weight in determining which nations progress beyond the group phase.

The match was played in Toronto as part of the tournament being co-hosted across North America. The 2026 World Cup represents the first edition featuring 48 teams, an expansion from the previous 32-team format. Ghana will look to build on this result in their remaining group matches, while Panama faces an uphill battle after the opening defeat.

cards.headline: Colombia defeats Uzbekistan in World Cup debut match
cards.teaser: Luis Diaz scored as Colombia beat World Cup debutants Uzbekistan 3-1 in their opening match of the tournament.
cards.body:
Colombia opened their World Cup campaign with a 3-1 victory over Uzbekistan in Mexico City. Daniel Muñoz scored a brilliant goal created by Luis Díaz, who was named man of the match. Jefferson Lerma controlled the midfield for Colombia, helping his team dominate much of the game.

Uzbekistan, competing in their first World Cup, showed resilience despite the defeat. Abbosbek Fayzullaev scored their inaugural World Cup goal, marking a historic moment for the Central Asian nation in their debut appearance.

cards.headline: England defeats Croatia in World Cup opener after halftime adjustments
cards.teaser: Thomas Tuchel delivered a halftime message to England players during their opening World Cup victory against Croatia.
cards.body:
England made a winning start to their World Cup campaign, beating Croatia 4-2 in an entertaining match in Dallas. The first half was chaotic, ending level at 2-2, with Harry Kane scoring both England goals—the first from a retaken penalty. Croatia's Martin Baturina and Petar Musa found the net for the visitors.

Manager Thomas Tuchel delivered a halftime message to his team, addressing their defensive vulnerabilities in open play. England improved significantly after the break, ultimately securing a commanding victory. Kane's performance and England's dominance on set pieces proved decisive as they opened their group stage campaign with three points.

cards.headline: Vancouver Goldeneyes select Caroline Harvey first overall in PWHL Draft
cards.teaser: The Vancouver Goldeneyes used the first pick in the 2026 PWHL Draft to select Caroline Harvey.
cards.body:
Original Card Text

Caroline Harvey became the top selection in the 2026 Professional Women's Hockey League Draft when the Vancouver Goldeneyes called her name with the first overall pick. The draft marked the latest step in building rosters for the league's teams as they prepare for upcoming competition.

Other teams made their selections throughout the draft, including the Boston Fleet choosing Grace Dwyer in the first round. The Toronto Sceptres acquired Kirsten Simms, while Detroit selected Swiss goalie Brndli to add international talent to their roster. The draft continued the league's expansion and development of professional women's hockey.

---

Note: The additional source material provided (articles about Elon Musk and European crime statistics) is unrelated to the PWHL Draft story, so I'm returning the original card text unchanged per your instructions.

cards.headline: Messi, Mbappe and Vinicius Jr score notable goals in World Cup opening round
cards.teaser: The first round of World Cup matches featured standout goals from Argentina's Lionel Messi, France's Kylian Mbappe and Brazil's Vinicius Jr.
cards.body:
Several of the world's top players delivered memorable goals during the opening round of World Cup group stage matches. Lionel Messi scored for Argentina, Kylian Mbappe found the net for France, and Vinicius Jr added a goal for Brazil. These strikes highlighted the individual talent on display as the tournament began.

All 48 teams completed their first matches in the expanded World Cup format. England secured a thrilling opening victory against Croatia, with Harry Kane scoring twice including from a retaken penalty, while Croatia's Martin Baturina and Petar Musa replied in a competitive 3-2 result.

cards.headline: Analysts rank all 48 World Cup teams after opening matches
cards.teaser: All 48 World Cup teams have completed their first group stage matches, prompting rankings from worst to best.
cards.body:
With all 48 teams having completed their opening matches, BBC Sport's experts have ranked every World Cup participant. Defending champions Argentina did not top the rankings despite their tournament favorites status. The assessment provides an early evaluation of team performances as competition progresses into subsequent group stage matches.

The expanded 48-team format requires comprehensive analysis across all participants compared to previous 32-team tournaments. Teams now advance with adjusted expectations based on their opening results and expert assessments.

cards.headline: United States prepares to face Australia in Seattle World Cup match
cards.teaser: The United States men's national team will play Australia in Seattle in an upcoming World Cup group stage match.
cards.body:
Seattle is preparing for a World Cup match between the United States and Australia. The game represents one of the busiest sporting events for the host city, which is also managing a Mariners doubleheader on the same day. The United States is competing in the World Cup as a co-host nation alongside Canada and Mexico.

Australia players have discussed their strategy for the match, including plans to counter American goalkeeper Patrick Freese. Some Australian players are club teammates with Freese, giving them familiarity with his style. The match will be broadcast on television with specific kick-off time and streaming options available for viewers.

hero.headline: Paramount Animation Developing Animated Survivor Movie With Jeff Probst
hero.body:
Paramount Animation is developing an animated comedy film based on the long-running reality competition series Survivor, with host Jeff Probst attached as executive producer. The project is being developed in partnership with CBS, which has broadcast the original series since 2000.

The animated film will feature animal contestants rather than human players. According to the official synopsis, the movie will be set on a remote and mystical island where animals from around the world compete against each other. The project marks an unusual crossroads between reality television and animated cinema, translating the survival competition format into a family-friendly animated feature.

Probst has hosted Survivor since its debut and has won multiple Emmy Awards for his work on the series. His involvement as executive producer brings continuity from the original show to the animated adaptation. The project represents Paramount Animation's latest effort to expand existing intellectual property from the ViacomCBS portfolio into new formats.

Survivor premiered in May 2000 and became a cultural phenomenon, helping to establish the reality competition genre on American television. The series places contestants in remote locations where they compete in challenges, form alliances, and vote each other out until one player remains. The show has aired more than 40 seasons and spawned numerous international versions.

The animated adaptation joins a growing trend of studios developing animated features based on established brands and television properties. Paramount Animation has previously worked on films including The SpongeBob Movie series and Paw Patrol: The Movie. No release date or additional production details for the Survivor animated film have been announced.

cards.headline: Guillermo Rodriguez Joins Dancing With the Stars Season 35
cards.teaser: The Jimmy Kimmel Live! personality will compete in the upcoming season of the dance competition series.
cards.body:
Guillermo Rodriguez, the sidekick on Jimmy Kimmel Live!, has joined the cast of Dancing With the Stars Season 35. Known for his comedic presence and tequila-fueled segments on the late-night show, Rodriguez will compete on the dance competition series for the first time.

Rodriguez joins other announced contestants including Maura Higgins from Love Island and The Traitors, and Ciara Miller from Summer House.

cards.headline: Lisa Kudrow Honored at Las Culturistas Culture Awards
cards.teaser: The actress received the Lifetime of Culture Award at the fifth annual comedy variety special hosted by Matt Rogers and Bowen Yang.
cards.body:
Lisa Kudrow received the Lifetime of Culture Award at the Las Culturistas Culture Awards, the fifth annual ceremony and second year to air on Bravo. The special is now streaming on Peacock. Comedians Matt Rogers and Bowen Yang hosted the event, which featured performances by Rachel Zegler and Mandy Moore.

Ben Platt performed a rendition of "Smelly Cat," the iconic song from Kudrow's character Phoebe Buffay on Friends. The performance incorporated marionettes created by the Bob Baker Marionettes.

cards.headline: Will Ferrell Honored as Titan of Culture at Las Culturistas Awards
cards.teaser: The actor received recognition from hosts Bowen Yang and Matt Rogers at the annual comedy awards show.
cards.body:
Will Ferrell was named a Titan of Culture at the 2026 Las Culturistas Awards, presented by podcast hosts and comedians Bowen Yang and Matt Rogers. Ferrell appeared at the ceremony wearing leather gear in recognition of Pride month.

During his appearance, Ferrell created a custom Pride flag that incorporated colors representing movies he has appeared in and references to his wealth. The Las Culturistas Culture Awards is an annual comedy variety special that honors figures in pop culture.

cards.headline: Spanish Publisher Promotes Literature as Source Material for Film and TV
cards.teaser: Fernando Benzo says books provide safe intellectual property for international adaptations as Spanish literature eyes global screen opportunities.
cards.body:
Spanish literature could become a major source for international film and television adaptations, according to Fernando Benzo, author and secretary general of the Spanish Federation of Publishers. Benzo told Variety that books represent safe intellectual property for screen development.

Benzo described the concept as fundamental to his perspective on the industry. He emphasized that books already have established fan bases when adapted for screen. The comments come as the Spanish publishing industry looks to expand its presence in global entertainment markets.

cards.headline: Olivia Wilde Responds to Criticism of Red Carpet Photo
cards.teaser: The actress addressed online reactions to a viral photograph that drew widespread commentary.
cards.body:
Olivia Wilde responded to criticism after a red carpet photograph sparked widespread online discussion. Critics commented on her appearance in the image, with some making extreme comparisons about how she looked in the photo.

Wilde addressed the reactions, calling the picture crazy. The photograph generated significant attention across social media platforms and entertainment news outlets. Multiple publications covered the online response to the image and Wilde's subsequent comments.

cards.headline: Mandy Moore Performs at Las Culturistas Culture Awards
cards.teaser: The singer and actress joined hosts Bowen Yang and Matt Rogers to perform Only Hope at the comedy awards show.
cards.body:
Mandy Moore performed "Only Hope" at the Las Culturistas Culture Awards, the fifth annual edition of the comedy variety special. The 2002 song was nominated for Record of the Year at the ceremony, which aired on Bravo and streams on Peacock.

The awards show was created by and hosted by Bowen Yang and Matt Rogers, who co-host the Las Culturistas podcast. The event celebrates achievements across pop culture with categories ranging from Album of the Year to more unconventional honors.

hero.headline: U.S. and Iran sign agreement to end war and reopen Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have signed a memorandum of understanding to end their conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. President Trump signed the document remotely, with the agreement now in effect. The signing happened ahead of a scheduled ceremony in Switzerland on Friday, after discussions among mediating countries about implementing the deal sooner.

The 14-paragraph memo includes an end to fighting, a commitment that Iran will never develop nuclear weapons, and a $300 billion redevelopment package for Iran. The deal aims to stabilize global energy markets after two months of military action that severely disrupted energy production and transportation across the Middle East.

Trump defended the agreement during an hour-long press conference, though he appeared to lower expectations for success. He warned he could authorize military strikes against Iran again if nuclear negotiations fail. Critics argue that making concessions simply to return to the pre-war situation demonstrates the conflict itself was a costly mistake. Before the war and as it began, Trump had outlined highly ambitious goals including Iran's total surrender and complete dismantling of its nuclear program.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has sharply criticized the deal, calling it a strategic and political disaster. Netanyahu had promised the Israeli public total victory but now faces Trump's diplomatic settlement and repeated public criticism from the president, occurring four months before an Israeli election. Netanyahu stands alone internationally in his opposition. Even the United Arab Emirates, previously the most hawkish Gulf state, supports the diplomatic resolution. Republican allies in Washington and the media have also been reluctant to fully reject a deal carrying Trump's approval.

The immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz faces significant delays. An estimated 5,000 mines that Iran placed in the waterway during the conflict must be swept before normal shipping traffic can resume. Trump said the U.S. military had already begun searching for mines, but the operation will require considerable time.

The conflict has created widespread economic damage globally. About 20,000 seafarers and 2,000 ships have been stranded in the Gulf. Germany halved its 2026 growth forecast to 0.5 percent on Wednesday, while Greece announced 500 million euros in extra aid for households and farmers. Countries in Asia dependent on Gulf oil have suffered particularly severe shortages of fuel, fertilizer, and other raw materials.

Peace negotiations remain fragile. Iran's parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that reopening the strait would be impossible while the U.S. and Israel committed breaches of the ceasefire, including the U.S. naval blockade. He accused them of "hostage-taking of the world's economy." Iran's military seized two ships attempting to cross the strait on Wednesday, marking the first vessel seizures since the war began on February 28.

cards.headline: New Jersey Democrat prepares bill requiring government reviews of advanced AI models
cards.teaser: Representative Josh Gottheimer plans legislation mandating federal reviews of powerful AI systems for national security and public safety risks.
cards.body:
Representative Josh Gottheimer is preparing legislation that would require advanced artificial intelligence models to undergo mandatory government reviews. The New Jersey Democrat's bill would focus on assessing risks to national security, critical infrastructure, and potential bioterrorism threats posed by powerful AI systems.

The proposed legislation represents a federal regulatory approach to AI safety as the technology continues to advance rapidly. Gottheimer's bill would establish a formal review process for AI models before deployment, marking a significant step toward government oversight of the artificial intelligence industry.

cards.headline: Poll shows two-thirds of Americans believe right to vote faces threat
cards.teaser: A new survey finds most Americans see various civil liberties, including voting rights, under some level of danger.
cards.body:
A majority of Americans express concern about the security of voting rights, according to a new AP-NORC Center survey. Two-thirds of respondents said the right to vote faces either a major or minor threat, while one-third believe voting rights are not under threat.

The poll reflects broader anxiety among the public about civil liberties in the country. Voting rights emerged as a particularly significant area of concern when researchers measured American perceptions of threats to various fundamental freedoms.

cards.headline: Senate pressures Defense Secretary Hegseth over Iran school attack and boat strikes
cards.teaser: Lawmakers are increasing demands for answers about apparent incidents during the Iran conflict that the Pentagon has not addressed for months.
cards.body:
Frustrated senators are targeting Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's travel and public schedule as they escalate pressure to obtain information about apparent Iranian attacks on a school and boat strikes during the recent conflict. Lawmakers say they have sought answers for months without receiving responses from the Pentagon.

The standoff reflects growing tensions between Congress and the Defense Department over transparency regarding incidents during the Iran war. Senate members are using their oversight authority to demand accountability from Hegseth on events that occurred during military operations.

cards.headline: Iranian mines in Strait of Hormuz delay reopening of shipping lane
cards.teaser: An estimated 5,000 mines placed during the war must be cleared before normal traffic can resume through the critical waterway.
cards.body:
Plans to quickly restore shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz are delayed by thousands of mines Iran placed in the waterway during the conflict. President Trump said the U.S. military had already begun searching for mines, estimating around 5,000 devices were deployed in the strait.

The mine-clearing operation will postpone the return to normal shipping operations despite the memorandum of understanding signed this week to end the war and reopen the critical passage. The strait serves as a vital route for global energy shipments, and the mines present a significant obstacle to implementing the agreement's economic provisions.

cards.headline: Former presidents Biden, Bush, and Clinton to attend Obama Presidential Center opening
cards.teaser: Three former presidents plan to attend the ceremony marking the opening of the center in Chicago.
cards.body:
Former Presidents Joe Biden, Bill Clinton, and George W. Bush plan to attend the opening of the Obama Presidential Center on Chicago's South Side. Former first ladies are also expected at the ceremony.

The $850 million center will showcase original artworks commissioned from 30 artists representing diverse backgrounds—a scale of artistic collaboration unprecedented at a presidential library. The opening is scheduled for mid-June, coinciding with the eve of Juneteenth.

cards.headline: Poll shows decline in American pride ahead of 250th anniversary
cards.teaser: Just over half of Americans say they are extremely or very proud of their American identity, according to new survey data.
cards.body:
Fifty-one percent of Americans say they are extremely proud or very proud of being from the United States, according to a new PRRI poll conducted ahead of the nation's 250th anniversary. Twenty-three percent said they are moderately proud of their American identity, while 14 percent reported lower levels of pride.

The survey reveals a decline in the proportion of Americans expressing high levels of national pride as the country approaches its semiquincentennial. The polling data suggests shifting attitudes about American identity among the population.
